options.title: Why is Lesotho surrounded by South Africa?
options.first_line: Why is Lesotho, a whole country, completely surrounded by South Africa?
options.first_frame: The old map of southern Africa: South Africa wearing its flag, and in its middle a small hole tracing itself in light as Lesotho, its own flag filling in.

options.title: A country you can only leave through South Africa?
options.first_line: Lesotho is a whole country you can only leave through South Africa. How did that happen?
options.first_frame: A truck at Lesotho's border gate on the map, every road out of the little mountain country running into South Africa, the gate lifting.

options.title: Why does South Africa have a hole in it?
options.first_line: Why does South Africa have a hole in the middle? That hole is a country, Lesotho.
options.first_frame: South Africa's whole shape on the map with a gap punched in its middle, the camera pushing in as the gap lights up and LESOTHO writes across it.

why: A hole punched in a country's map is a picture anyone gets with the sound off and an instant 'how is that possible?', and revealing it is Lesotho only sharpens the real question, why, which the viewer must stay for.
